biography_sections.title: Newspaper evidence and profile attribution
biography_sections.markdown:
The profile assignment remains qualified. James McClure Glasgow-1780 (1805–1890) is a strong compatible candidate: his live biography expressly names the Royal Belfast Academical Institution and mathematical distinction. That current-profile statement is a comparison, not a newly inspected primary education source. The newspaper’s James has no age or relatives. Co-occurrence with Adam does not independently prove siblinghood; other namesakes are not excluded merely for missing fields.

Adam D. Glasgow of Broughshane appears in the Royal Belfast Academical Institution school prizes in June 1830 and Belfast College examinations reported in May 1831. The 1831 report also names James Glasgow, Institution, in voluntary advanced mathematical examinations. [Belfast News-Letter, 29 June 1830, p.3, Royal Belfast Academical Institution School Department](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390569859/) · [Belfast News-Letter, 6 May 1831, p.3, Belfast College report dated 30 April](https://www.newspapers.com/image/390545285/)

[Complete newspaper account and held draft](/research/subjects/newspapers-irish-1800-1850/#james-belfast-college). Read the primary education source behind James-1780’s current biography and check the Institution examination/admission registers. Do not make the newspaper co-occurrence a new sibling proof.
